text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- National statistics office INSEE forecasts for the first half of 1997 a 0.9 percent rise in GDP, due to a better international context, renewed investments, but expects a 13 percent unemployment rate through June 1997. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- CNPF emplouyers' federation holds annual general meeting today.
-- TPS digital TV joint venture managing director Cyrille du Peloux says in an interview that he expects competition with subscriber-TV channel Canal Plus to boost digital TV market in France.
-- Court orders retail group Intermarche to reimburse suppliers for illegal price cuts.
-- Report urges businesses to hold their accounts in euros as early as 1997, to ease transition to a single currency in 1999.
-- A Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger to create a 250-billion-franc turnover group, puts pressure on Europe, which is currently engaged in a restructuring of its aircraft industry.
-- Furniture and tools group Strafor Facom sells bakery equipment unit Bongard, expects a 200-million-franc profit for 1996.
-- Auchan supermarkets group chairman Francis Cordelette in an interview says will reorganise newly acquired Docks de France .
-- Banks cut base lending rate to 6.30 from 6.55, thanks to the sound situation of French markets after news that European leaders had reached an agreement on a monetary "stability pact".
-- State-owned post office La Poste chairman resigns, Claude Bourmaud to succeed him.
-- Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger may speed a planned shift in status at Airbus consortium to that of a limited company.
-- South Korea considers trade retaliation measures against France after failure of Daewoo's bid to takeover Thomson Multimedia.
